summary: Alabama requires a rear-facing seat until at least age 1 or 20 pounds, a forward-facing seat until at least age 5 or 40 pounds, a booster until age 6, and a seat belt until age 15.
rear_facing_rule: Infant-only seats and convertible seats used in the rear-facing position for infants until at least one year of age or 20 pounds.
harness_rule: Convertible seats in the forward position or forward-facing seats until the child is at least five years of age or 40 pounds.
booster_rule: Booster seats until the child is six years of age.
seat_belt_rule: Seat belts until 15 years of age, so children 6 through 14 must be buckled in a seat belt.
back_seat_rule: Alabama law doesn't say where in the car a child must sit.
penalty: Up to $25 per offense. The judge may dismiss the charge, with no court costs, on proof that you've acquired an appropriate child restraint. 1 point on a first offense, 2 points on a second or later offense.
exemptions: Does not apply to taxis or to vehicles that seat 11 or more passengers. The law covers passenger cars, pickup trucks, vans seating 10 or fewer, minivans and SUVs.
agency: Alabama Law Enforcement Agency; Alabama Department of Public Health

summary: Alaska requires a rear-facing seat for babies under 1 and for any child who weighs under 20 pounds, a car seat from age 1 to 4, and a booster from age 4 to 8 until the child reaches 57 inches or 65 pounds. Every child under 16 must be restrained.
rear_facing_rule: A child less than one year old, or one year or older who weighs less than 20 pounds, must ride in a rear-facing child safety seat used according to the manufacturer's instructions.
harness_rule: A child one year or older but under four who weighs 20 pounds or more must ride in a child restraint device used according to the manufacturer's instructions. The law doesn't specify a harness.
booster_rule: A child over four but under eight who is under 57 inches tall and weighs at least 20 but less than 65 pounds must ride in a booster seat secured by a seat belt, or in another child restraint system.
seat_belt_rule: A child over four who exceeds the booster height or weight limits (57 inches or 65 pounds) must wear a seat belt. Children 8 to 15 who are still under those limits ride in a child safety device or a seat belt, whichever the driver decides is appropriate.
back_seat_rule: Alaska law doesn't say where in the car a child must sit.
penalty: The court bail schedule sets $50 for failing to provide a child safety device and $50 for failing to properly secure a child in one. A first charge for failing to provide a device may be dismissed on proof of correction; a second or later charge may not.
exemptions: School buses (unless federally required to have belts), emergency vehicles, mail and newspaper delivery from inside the vehicle, vehicles not equipped with seat belts, people exempted by regulation, and motorcycles, off-highway vehicles and similar vehicles.
agency: Alaska Highway Safety Office (Department of Transportation & Public Facilities)

summary: Arizona requires children under 5 to ride in a child restraint system, and children 5 through 7 who are 4'9" or shorter to ride in a child restraint system such as a booster. There is no rear-facing requirement.
rear_facing_rule: Arizona law has no rear-facing requirement.
harness_rule: Children under five must be properly secured in a child restraint system. The law's definition of child restraint system includes booster seats, so it doesn't require a harnessed seat by age.
booster_rule: Each passenger at least five but under eight years old who is not more than four feet nine inches tall must ride in a child restraint system (the definition includes booster seats).
seat_belt_rule: Children 5 through 7 who are taller than 4'9" may use the seat belt. Arizona's separate seat belt law covers older children.
back_seat_rule: Arizona law doesn't say where in the car a child must sit.
penalty: Civil penalty of $50, which is not imposed if you show the vehicle has since been equipped with a compliant child restraint system (for example, a receipt mailed to the court). The Governor's Office of Highway Safety notes that with court surcharges the total is often well over $100 in many jurisdictions, and that a Children Are Priceless Passengers class (a $35 fee that includes a seat if needed) can reduce the citation.
exemptions: Vehicles originally made without passenger restraints, recreational vehicles, commercial vehicles driven by a CDL holder, emergencies to get medical care, emergency vehicles taking a child for medical care, and cars too small to fit all the seats needed (if at least one child and as many others as reasonable are restrained).
agency: Arizona Governor's Office of Highway Safety

summary: Arkansas requires a child under 6 who weighs less than 60 pounds to ride in a child passenger safety seat. Once a child is 6 or weighs 60 pounds, a seat belt is enough, and every child under 15 must be restrained.
rear_facing_rule: Arkansas law has no rear-facing requirement.
harness_rule: The law requires a 'child passenger safety seat' (see the booster row) but doesn't specify a harnessed seat or a booster.
booster_rule: A child who is less than six years of age and who weighs less than sixty pounds shall be restrained in a child passenger safety seat properly secured to the vehicle.
seat_belt_rule: If a child is at least six years of age or at least 60 pounds, a safety belt properly secured to the vehicle meets the law. Drivers must restrain every child under 15.
back_seat_rule: Arkansas law doesn't say where in the car a child must sit.
penalty: Fine of not less than $25 nor more than $100. If you show the court you have since acquired, purchased or rented an approved child passenger safety seat, the court may assess no more than the minimum fine. The court also considers whether the child was restrained by some other means, such as a seat belt.
exemptions: Vehicles operated for hire. The law covers passenger cars, vans and pickup trucks.
agency: Arkansas Department of Public Safety

summary: California requires rear-facing until age 2 (unless the child is 40+ pounds or 40+ inches), a car seat or booster in the back seat until age 8 or 4'9", and a restraint or seat belt through age 15. From January 1, 2027, a child 8 to 15 may use the belt alone only if they pass the 5-step test.
rear_facing_rule: A child under two must ride in a rear-facing child passenger restraint system unless the child weighs 40 or more pounds or is 40 or more inches tall, secured within the seat maker's height and weight limits.
harness_rule: California law doesn't set an age for moving from a five-point harness to a booster (the CHP says the law does not address it).
booster_rule: A child under eight must be properly secured in a rear seat in an appropriate child passenger restraint system. A child under eight who is 4'9" or taller may use a safety belt instead.
seat_belt_rule: Children 8 through 15 must be secured in an appropriate child passenger restraint system or a safety belt. A child over 40 pounds may wear only a lap belt in the back seat if it has no lap-and-shoulder belt.
back_seat_rule: Children under 8 must ride in the rear seat. Exceptions: no rear seat, side-facing jump seats, rear-facing rear seats, the restraint can't be installed properly in back, all rear seats are taken by children 7 or under, or a medical reason. A rear-facing seat may never go in front of an active frontal passenger airbag.
penalty: $100 for a first offense and $250 for a second or later one (before court penalty assessments). The court may reduce or waive the fine for an economically disadvantaged defendant who completes a community child passenger safety education program.
exemptions: The court may exempt a child whose physical unfitness, medical condition or size makes a restraint impractical. Life-threatening emergencies and authorized emergency vehicles are exempt when no restraint is available (the child must use a seat belt). The section doesn't apply to a driver when the child's parent or legal guardian is a passenger.
pending_change: AB 435 (Stats. 2025, Ch. 434) takes effect January 1, 2027. A child 8 to 15, or a child under 8 who is 4'9" or taller, will count as 'properly restrained by a safety belt' only if they pass all five steps of the 5-step test: sitting all the way back against the seat, knees bending over the seat edge, shoulder belt snug across the center of the chest and shoulder and not the neck, lap belt as low as possible and touching the thighs, and able to stay seated like this for the whole trip. Otherwise they must stay in a child passenger restraint system such as a booster.
agency: California Highway Patrol

summary: Colorado requires rear-facing until age 2 (unless the child weighs 40+ pounds), a rear- or forward-facing car seat from 2 to 4, a car seat or booster until age 9, and the back seat (if there is one) until age 9. Children 9 through 17 need a belt or child restraint.
rear_facing_rule: A child under two must ride in a rear seat if one is available, rear-facing if the child weighs under 40 pounds; at 40 pounds or more, rear- or forward-facing.
harness_rule: A child two or older but under four who weighs at least 20 pounds must ride in a rear-facing or forward-facing child restraint system, in the rear seat if available.
booster_rule: Every child under nine must be properly restrained in a child restraint system per the manufacturer's instructions. A child four or older but under nine who weighs at least 40 pounds must ride in a child restraint system or booster seat, in the rear seat if available.
seat_belt_rule: Children 9 through 17 (until their 18th birthday) must use a safety belt or child restraint system. CDOT says a child can stop using a booster only at age 9 and only if the belt fits properly.
back_seat_rule: Children under 9 must ride in the rear seat if one is available.
penalty: A class B traffic infraction: $65 penalty plus a $16 surcharge on the state schedule. The fine may be waived if you show the court, by your court appearance, that you've acquired, purchased or rented a child restraint system.
exemptions: A child under 9 in a medical or other life-threatening emergency when no restraint is available; commercial vehicles operated by a child care center; for-hire common or contract carriers and luxury limousines. CDOT notes that buses, shuttle vans and taxis are exempt.
agency: Colorado Department of Transportation

summary: Connecticut requires rear-facing with a 5-point harness until age 2 and 30 pounds, a 5-point harness until age 5 and 40 pounds, and a harness or booster until age 8 and 60 pounds. After that, a belt or child restraint through age 15.
rear_facing_rule: A child under two years of age or weighing less than thirty pounds must ride rear-facing in a child restraint system equipped with a five-point harness.
harness_rule: A child under five (but not under two), or weighing less than forty pounds (but not less than thirty), must ride rear- or forward-facing in a child restraint system with a five-point harness.
booster_rule: A child under eight (but not under five), or weighing less than sixty pounds (but not less than forty), must ride in a five-point-harness seat or a booster seat secured by a seat safety belt. A booster may be used only with a belt that includes a shoulder belt.
seat_belt_rule: A child eight or older and weighing 60 pounds or more may use an approved child restraint or a seat safety belt. Drivers must secure passengers 8 to 15 in a seat belt.
back_seat_rule: No back seat rule, but a rear-facing seat may not go in the front seat of a vehicle with a functional passenger-side air bag.
penalty: A first violation is an infraction; a second is a fine of up to $199; a third or later is a class A misdemeanor. Anyone with a first or second violation must take a DMV child car seat safety course, and the DMV may suspend the license for up to two months for skipping it. The court may remit a first-time fine if you show proof within 14 days that you acquired, rented or bought an appropriate seat.
exemptions: Children in student transportation vehicles follow separate rules (age 4 and up may use a belt). The child restraint rules don't apply on buses of one ton or more.
agency: Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles

summary: Delaware requires a rear-facing 5-point-harness seat for children under 2 and under 30 pounds, a 5-point harness for children under 4 and under 40 pounds, and a booster until the child outgrows it. Children under 12 who are 5'5" or shorter can't ride in front of an active air bag.
rear_facing_rule: A child under the age of 2 years and less than 30 pounds must be properly secured in a rear-facing child restraint equipped with a 5-point harness.
harness_rule: A child under the age of 4 and less than 40 pounds must be properly secured in a 5-point-harness restraint, rear- or forward-facing, until reaching the restraint's upper height or weight limits.
booster_rule: A child must be properly secured in a belt-positioning booster until reaching the booster's upper height or weight limits per the manufacturer's guidelines.
seat_belt_rule: A child who has reached the booster's upper height and weight limits and is under 16 must wear a properly secured seat belt in every seating position.
back_seat_rule: A child under 12 who is 5'5" or shorter may not ride in the front passenger seat of a vehicle with an active passenger-side air bag, unless there's no rear seat or all rear seats are taken by other such children. This is a secondary offense.
penalty: A first offense brings no fine: police should refer the driver to an Office of Highway Safety car seat fitting station. A second or later violation is a $25 fine (plus court costs, per OHS).
exemptions: Charter buses, limousines and taxicabs.
agency: Delaware Office of Highway Safety

summary: D.C. requires rear-facing until age 2 (unless the child is at least 40 pounds and 40 inches), a car seat until age 3, and an infant, convertible or booster seat until age 8. Children 8 to 15 need a seat belt or child restraint.
rear_facing_rule: A child under 2 who weighs less than 40 pounds or measures less than 40 inches must be properly restrained in a rear-facing child restraint seat.
harness_rule: A child under 3 must be properly restrained in a child restraint seat (one fastened to the vehicle by a seat belt, with all its securing straps in use).
booster_rule: Children under 8 must be properly seated in an installed infant, convertible (toddler) or booster child safety seat, according to the manufacturer's instructions. A booster may only be used with both a lap and shoulder belt.
seat_belt_rule: Every child under 16 must be restrained in an approved child safety restraint system or a seat belt, so children 8 to 15 may use the belt.
back_seat_rule: No general back seat rule. A parent carrying more of their own children than there are belts may leave some unrestrained, but an unrestrained child may not ride in the front seat.
penalty: First offense: pay a $75 fine or attend a child restraint safety class ($25). Second: the class ($25) plus a $75 fine. Third: $125. Fourth and later: $150. Processed as a moving violation, with 2 points. The fine for a first violation of the under-3 rule is waived with proof you've since acquired an approved seat (purchase, gift or loan program).
exemptions: The law applies to personal-use vehicles seating 8 or fewer passengers; it excludes livery, sightseeing, taxi, ambulance, funeral and farm vehicles.
agency: District Department of Transportation (Child Safety Seat Program)

summary: Florida requires children through age 3 to ride in a separate carrier or integrated child seat, and children 4 and 5 to ride in a carrier, integrated seat or booster. From age 6, a seat belt is allowed. There is no rear-facing requirement.
rear_facing_rule: Florida law has no rear-facing requirement.
harness_rule: For children aged through 3 years, the restraint must be a separate carrier or a vehicle manufacturer's integrated child seat.
booster_rule: For children aged 4 through 5 years, a separate carrier, an integrated child seat, or a child booster seat may be used.
seat_belt_rule: Children 6 and older may use a seat belt, and all passengers under 18 must be belted or in a child restraint. A 4- or 5-year-old may use a seat belt instead only when carried free by a driver outside the immediate family, in a medical emergency, or with documented medical need.
back_seat_rule: No Florida law says where in the car a child must sit.
penalty: A moving violation with a $60 base fine and 3 points on your license. With the court's approval, you can instead complete a child restraint safety program; then the points are waived and the fine and costs may be waived.
exemptions: For-hire chauffeur-driven taxis, limousines, sedans, vans, buses and motor coaches; school buses; buses for hire; farm equipment; trucks over 26,000 lb GVWR; motorcycles, mopeds and bicycles. Ages 4-5 may use a belt in the three situations above.
agency: Florida Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles

summary: Georgia requires children under 8 to ride in a car seat or booster suited to their height and weight, in the back seat. A child under 8 who is over 4'9" may use a seat belt instead.
rear_facing_rule: Georgia law has no rear-facing requirement.
harness_rule: The law requires a child passenger restraining system appropriate for the child's height and weight (see the booster row), not a specific seat type.
booster_rule: A child under 8 must be properly restrained in a child passenger restraining system appropriate for their height and weight, approved under FMVSS 213 and used per the manufacturer's directions. If the child's height is over 4'9", a seat belt is required instead.
seat_belt_rule: Every minor 8 or older must wear a seat belt. A child under 8 who weighs at least 40 pounds may use a lap belt only when the vehicle has no lap-and-shoulder belts, or when they're all in use by other children.
back_seat_rule: A child under 8 must ride in a rear seat, unless the vehicle has no rear seat suitable for a car seat or all of them are taken by other children.
penalty: First conviction: fine of not more than $50. Second or later: not more than $100. No court may add fees or surcharges. 1 point on a first offense, 2 points on a second or later offense.
exemptions: Taxicabs and public transit vehicles; the rule covers passenger cars, vans and pickup trucks, and multifunction school activity buses need not carry children 5 or older in a car seat. A physician's written statement that a child's physical or medical condition prevents restraint.
agency: Governor's Office of Highway Safety (Georgia)

summary: Hawaii requires rear-facing with a harness under age 2, a rear- or forward-facing harness seat from 2 to 4, and a harness seat or booster from 4 to 10. Children 7 to 9 who are over 4'9" may use a lap-and-shoulder belt.
rear_facing_rule: A child under two must be properly restrained in a rear-facing child passenger restraint system with harness.
harness_rule: A child two or older but under four must be properly restrained in a rear- or forward-facing child passenger restraint system with harness.
booster_rule: A child four or older but under ten must be properly restrained in a harnessed child restraint or booster seat. A child seven or older but under ten who is over four feet nine inches may instead use a lap-and-shoulder belt.
seat_belt_rule: Children 7 to 9 who are over 4'9" may use a correctly worn lap-and-shoulder belt. From age 10, the child restraint law no longer applies.
back_seat_rule: Hawaii law doesn't say where in the car a child must sit.
penalty: First conviction: fine up to $100, a required child passenger restraint safety class (up to four hours), a $50 driver education assessment, a $10 neurotrauma surcharge, and up to a $10 trauma system surcharge. Second within three years: $250 to $500. Third or later within three years: $500 to $800.
exemptions: Emergency, commercial (for-hire) and mass transit vehicles, plus any exemptions the Department of Transportation sets by rule.
agency: Hawaii Department of Transportation

summary: Idaho requires children 6 and younger to ride in a child safety restraint that meets federal standard FMVSS 213. From age 7, the regular seat belt law applies. There is no rear-facing or back seat requirement.
rear_facing_rule: Idaho law has no rear-facing requirement.
harness_rule: The law requires a child safety restraint (see the booster row) but doesn't specify a harness or booster.
booster_rule: A child six years of age or younger must be properly secured in a child safety restraint that meets federal motor vehicle safety standard no. 213 (car seats and boosters both meet it).
seat_belt_rule: From age 7, every occupant must wear a safety restraint under Idaho's seat belt law.
back_seat_rule: No general rule. If all seat belts are in use and a child goes unrestrained, that child must be placed in the rear seat if the vehicle has one.
penalty: The Idaho Supreme Court infraction schedule sets a $84 total: a $27.50 fixed penalty plus court costs and fees.
exemptions: Applies only to noncommercial drivers in vehicles made with seat belts after January 1, 1966. Exempt when all seat belts are in use (the unrestrained child goes in back), and while a child is out of the seat for nursing or other immediate physiological needs.
agency: Idaho Transportation Department, Office of Highway Safety

summary: Illinois requires rear-facing until age 2 (unless the child is 40+ pounds or 40+ inches) and an appropriate child restraint, which can be a booster, until age 8. Children 8 to 15 must wear a seat belt.
rear_facing_rule: A child under 2 must be properly secured in a rear-facing child restraint system, unless the child weighs 40 or more pounds or is 40 or more inches tall.
harness_rule: Illinois law doesn't require a harnessed seat by age. Children under 8 need an appropriate child restraint system, which includes boosters (see the booster row).
booster_rule: A child under 8 must be properly secured in an appropriate child restraint system ('which also includes a booster seat'). The parent or guardian must give anyone transporting their child under 8 a child restraint system.
seat_belt_rule: Children 8 through 15 must be secured in seat belts. A child over 40 pounds may ride in the back seat with only a lap belt if the back seat has no lap-and-shoulder belt.
back_seat_rule: No Illinois law says where in the car a child must sit.
penalty: First violation: a petty offense with a $75 fine. Second or later: $200. On a first violation of the under-8 rule, you won't be convicted if you show the court you have an approved child restraint and completed an installation course with a certified technician.
exemptions: A child whose physical disability prevents appropriate restraint, certified by a physician.
agency: Illinois Department of Transportation

summary: Indiana requires children under 8 to ride in a child restraint system, which can be a booster, used per the manufacturer's instructions. Children 8 to 15 need a child restraint or seat belt. There is no rear-facing requirement.
rear_facing_rule: Indiana law has no rear-facing requirement.
harness_rule: Indiana law doesn't require a harnessed seat by age; the under-8 rule (see the booster row) covers any child restraint system.
booster_rule: A child less than eight must be properly fastened and restrained by a child restraint system according to the manufacturer's instructions. The state says this can include a belt-positioning booster.
seat_belt_rule: Children 8 through 15 must be properly fastened in a child restraint system or a safety belt. A child over 40 pounds may use a lap belt if the vehicle has no lap-and-shoulder belts, or if all of them outside the front seats are in use by other children.
back_seat_rule: No Indiana law says where in the car a child must sit.
penalty: A Class D infraction, with a judgment of up to $25. If it's your first violation and you have or acquire a child restraint system, you're not liable for any costs or monetary judgment.
exemptions: A child with a physical or medical condition that makes a restraint impractical, if the driver carries a certificate from a physician, physician assistant or advanced practice registered nurse and shows it to the officer or court.
agency: Indiana Criminal Justice Institute (Traffic Safety)

summary: Iowa requires a rear-facing seat for a child under 1 who weighs under 20 pounds, a child restraint system (a booster counts) until age 6, and a restraint or seat belt from 6 through 17.
rear_facing_rule: A child under one year of age and weighing less than twenty pounds must be secured in a rear-facing child restraint system used according to the manufacturer's instructions.
harness_rule: Iowa law doesn't require a harnessed seat by age. The under-6 rule (see the booster row) covers any child restraint system, including boosters.
booster_rule: A child under six years of age must be secured by a child restraint system used according to the manufacturer's instructions. The definition includes belt-positioning and booster seats.
seat_belt_rule: A child at least six but under eighteen must be secured by a child restraint system or by a safety belt or safety harness.
back_seat_rule: No Iowa law says where in the car a child must sit.
penalty: A simple misdemeanor with a scheduled fine of $135. If it's your first charge under the age-6 rules and you had no child restraint, you won't be convicted if you show the court in time that you've since bought or acquired one.
exemptions: Peace officers on duty; 1965 or older vehicles, emergency vehicles, buses, motor homes and motorsports recreational vehicles (except the front passenger seat); a child certified by a physician or physician assistant as having a condition that prevents restraint; and back seat riders when all belts are in use. In a taxi or rideshare, the parent or adult with the child gets the ticket.
agency: Iowa Department of Public Safety, Governor's Traffic Safety Bureau

summary: Kansas requires children under 4 to ride in a child safety seat meeting FMVSS 213, and children 4 to 7 to keep using one (a booster qualifies) until they reach 80 pounds or 4'9". Children 8 to 13 must wear a seat belt.
rear_facing_rule: Kansas law has no rear-facing requirement.
harness_rule: A child under four must use an appropriate child passenger safety restraining system meeting FMVSS 213. The law doesn't say harness, and the same wording covers the 4-7 tier.
booster_rule: A child four or older but under eight 'who weighs less than 80 pounds or is less than 4 feet 9 inches in height' must use an appropriate child passenger safety restraining system meeting FMVSS 213, such as a booster.
seat_belt_rule: A child eight or older but under 14, 'or who weighs more than 80 pounds or is more than 4 feet 9 inches in height', must wear a safety belt. If a seat has only a lap belt, a child who would otherwise need a booster must use the lap belt.
back_seat_rule: No Kansas law says where in the car a child must sit.
penalty: A $60 fine, waived for the under-8 rules if you show the court you've bought or acquired an appropriate seat (the officer must tell you this). Not counted as a moving violation. Multiple unrestrained children in one car count as one violation.
exemptions: No violation if there are more children needing restraint than seating positions and all positions are in use by children. The law covers passenger cars and autocycles.
agency: Kansas Department of Transportation (Kansas Traffic Safety Resource Office)

summary: Kentucky requires a car seat for children 40 inches tall or shorter, and a booster seat for children under 8 who are between 40 and 57 inches tall. The law has no rear-facing or back-seat requirement.
rear_facing_rule: Kentucky law does not require rear-facing. The Office of Highway Safety's fact sheet advises rear-facing to at least age 1 and 20 pounds, with age 2 and 30 pounds as best practice.
harness_rule: A child 40 inches tall or shorter must be properly secured in a child restraint system that meets federal motor vehicle safety standards. The law sets this by height, not age.
booster_rule: A child under 8 who is between 40 and 57 inches tall must be properly secured in a child booster seat. A child of any age taller than 57 inches does not need a booster.
seat_belt_rule: In a vehicle made after 1981, the driver and all passengers must wear a properly adjusted and fastened seat belt, unless the passenger is a child secured in a car seat or booster as the law requires.
back_seat_rule: No Kentucky law says where in the car a child must sit.
penalty: Not using a required car seat carries a $50 fine. Not using a required booster carries a $30 fine. Neither fine adds court costs or fees. A first-time booster violator can have the charge dismissed, with no fees or costs, by showing proof they acquired a booster seat.
exemptions: The section's definition of motor vehicle excludes motorcycles, motor-driven cycles, farm trucks registered for agricultural use only with a gross weight of one ton or more, and vehicles designed to carry more than 15 passengers.
agency: Kentucky Transportation Cabinet, Office of Highway Safety

summary: Louisiana requires rear-facing until at least age 2, a harnessed forward-facing seat until at least age 4, then a booster until at least age 9 or until the child outgrows it. Children under 13 must ride in the back seat when one is available.
rear_facing_rule: A child younger than 2 must ride in a rear-facing child restraint until reaching the seat manufacturer's weight or height limit.
harness_rule: A child at least 2 who has outgrown the rear-facing limits must ride in a forward-facing seat with an internal harness until reaching that seat's weight or height limit. The booster stage starts only at age 4 or older.
booster_rule: A child at least 4 who has outgrown the forward-facing harness limits must ride in a belt-positioning booster with a lap-shoulder belt. A child moves to the adult belt at age 9, or sooner after outgrowing the booster's height or weight limits.
seat_belt_rule: A child at least 9, or one who has outgrown the booster's limits, must use the adult seat belt fitted correctly: sitting all the way back, knees bent over the seat edge, lap belt across the thighs and lower hips, and shoulder belt across the center of the chest. The law covers all children under 18.
back_seat_rule: A child younger than 13 must ride in the rear seat when one is available. If an active passenger air bag is present, a child younger than 6 or under 60 pounds must ride in the rear seat if one is available.
penalty: A first offense is a $100 fine. A second offense is $250 to $500, and a third or later offense is $500 plus court costs. If the only violation is using the wrong restraint for an otherwise restrained child, the fine is capped at $100, fees and court costs included. A violation is not a moving violation. Having no restraint at all is a primary offense. Using the wrong-size restraint is a secondary offense: a driver can be cited for it only when stopped for a moving violation.
exemptions: The law does not apply to ambulances or other emergency vehicles, during an emergency that threatens a life, or to a child who for medical reasons cannot use a restraint. The definition of motor vehicle excludes school buses, church and private buses and RVs with more than 10 seats, commercial trucks, vans and taxis, trucks rated over 2,000 lb capacity, farm tractors and motorcycles.
agency: Louisiana Highway Safety Commission

summary: Maine requires rear-facing under age 2 and a harnessed seat for children 2 and older who weigh less than 55 pounds. After that, a booster is required until the child is 8, 57 inches tall or 80 pounds. Children under 12 must ride in the rear seat if possible.
rear_facing_rule: A child under 2 must ride in a rear-facing seat, or a convertible seat in the rear-facing position. A child in a convertible seat who exceeds its rear-facing weight or height limit may face forward.
harness_rule: A child 2 or older who weighs less than 55 pounds must ride in a child restraint with an internal harness. If the child exceeds the harness seat's height limit first, they move to a federally approved belt-positioning seat.
booster_rule: A child who weighs less than 80 pounds, is shorter than 57 inches and is under 8 must ride in a belt-positioning seat or other child restraint. A child who reaches any one of those limits may use a seat belt.
seat_belt_rule: A child under 18 who is not required to use a car seat or booster must be properly secured in a seat belt. Passengers 18 and older and the driver must also be belted.
back_seat_rule: The driver must ensure that a child under 12 is properly secured in the rear seat, if possible.
penalty: Each violation is a traffic infraction with a mandatory fine: $50 for a first offense, $125 for a second and $250 for a third or later offense. The court may not suspend the fine.
exemptions: The car seat and booster rules don't apply to a child whose medical condition calls for a different restraint. That opinion must be in writing from a physician, nurse practitioner, physician associate, or child passenger safety technician with special needs training, must recommend the restraint and must explain why. The child must then ride in the recommended restraint.
agency: Maine Department of Public Safety, Bureau of Highway Safety

summary: Maryland requires children under 2 to ride rear-facing, and children under 8 to ride in a car seat or booster unless they are 4 feet 9 inches or taller. Every child under 16 must use a car seat, booster or seat belt.
rear_facing_rule: A child under 2 must ride in a rear-facing child safety seat until reaching the seat manufacturer's weight or height limit.
harness_rule: Maryland law has no separate harness stage. Children under 8 must ride in a child safety seat, which can be a harnessed seat or a booster, following the seat and vehicle instructions.
booster_rule: A child under 8 must ride in a child safety seat, booster seats included, unless the child is 4 feet 9 inches or taller.
seat_belt_rule: A child under 16 must be secured in a child safety seat or a seat belt. A seat belt may not be used for more than one person at a time.
back_seat_rule: No Maryland law says where in the car a child must sit. The health department notes that a rear-facing seat may not be placed in front of an active air bag.
penalty: A violation carries a $50 fine. A first violation of the rear-facing rule (a child under 2 in a seat that isn't rear-facing) gets a written warning. A judge may waive the fine if the driver had no car seat at the time, gets one before the hearing and shows proof to the court. A violation is not a moving violation, so it adds no points. Failing to restrain several children in the same trip counts as a single violation.
exemptions: Not a violation if a physician licensed in the state where the vehicle is registered certifies in writing that a car seat is impractical for the child because of weight, height, physical unfitness or another medical reason. The law covers Class A (passenger), Class E (truck) and Class M (multipurpose) vehicles. The health department says taxis are exempt and ride-share vehicles are not.
agency: Maryland Department of Health, Kids In Safety Seats (KISS)

summary: Massachusetts requires children under 8 to ride in a car seat or booster unless they are more than 57 inches tall. Children under 13 who have outgrown that requirement must wear a seat belt.
rear_facing_rule: Massachusetts law does not require rear-facing.
harness_rule: Massachusetts law has no separate harness stage. Children under 8 must ride in a federally approved child passenger restraint, either a car seat or a booster.
booster_rule: A passenger under 8 must be secured in a child passenger restraint, fastened according to the manufacturer's instructions, unless the child is more than 57 inches tall.
seat_belt_rule: A passenger under 13 who is not required to use a child passenger restraint must wear a properly adjusted and fastened safety belt.
back_seat_rule: No Massachusetts law says where in the car a child must sit.
penalty: A driver who violates the law faces a fine of up to $25. The fine does not apply to a taxi driver whose cab has no child restraint. A violation is not counted as a moving violation for car-insurance surcharge purposes, and a citation can be contested.
exemptions: The law does not apply to a child riding a school bus, a child in a vehicle made before July 1, 1966 that has no seat belts, or a child a physician certifies in writing as physically unable to use a conventional or special-needs restraint.
agency: Commonwealth of Massachusetts (Mass.gov)

summary: Since April 2, 2025, Michigan requires rear-facing until age 2, a harnessed forward-facing seat until age 5, and a booster until age 8 or 4 feet 9 inches. Each stage can end sooner if the child reaches the seat's limits. Children under 13 must ride in the rear seat if the vehicle has one.
rear_facing_rule: A child must ride rear-facing until reaching the seat manufacturer's rear-facing weight or height limit or turning 2, whichever comes first.
harness_rule: A child must then ride in a forward-facing seat with an internal harness until reaching that seat's weight or height limit or turning 5, whichever comes first.
booster_rule: A child must then ride in a belt-positioning booster with a lap-shoulder belt until reaching 4 feet 9 inches or turning 8.
seat_belt_rule: A child who is 8 or older, or 4 feet 9 inches or taller, and under 13 must wear a properly adjusted and fastened safety belt, and may keep using a booster within its limits. Children 13 to 15 must be belted under § 257.710e, which also requires the driver and front-seat passengers to wear belts.
back_seat_rule: Children under 13 must ride in a rear seat if the vehicle has one. A child may sit in front only if all available rear seats are occupied by children. A rear-facing seat may go in front only if the passenger air bag is turned off.
penalty: A violation is a civil infraction with a fine of up to $10 plus court costs. No points are assessed, and no abstract goes to the Secretary of State. The court may waive the fine, costs and assessments if, before the appearance date, the driver shows proof of getting a compliant car seat and of receiving education from a certified child passenger safety technician.
exemptions: The law does not apply in a bus, school bus, taxicab, moped, motorcycle or any vehicle not required to have seat belts under federal law. The Secretary of State may exempt, by rule, children for whom a car seat is impractical because of physical unfitness, a medical problem or body size.
agency: Michigan State Police, Office of Highway Safety Planning

summary: Children ride rear-facing until at least age 2, in a harnessed seat until at least 4, and in a booster until 9 or until they outgrow it; each move up happens only after the child outgrows the current seat's height or weight limit. Children under 13 must ride in the back seat when one is available.
rear_facing_rule: A child under 2 must be properly restrained in a rear-facing child restraint with an internal harness until the child reaches that seat's height or weight limit.
harness_rule: A child at least 2 who has outgrown the rear-facing seat must ride forward-facing with an internal harness until reaching that seat's height or weight limit. A booster is allowed only from age 4, after the child outgrows the forward-facing seat.
booster_rule: A child at least 4 who has outgrown the forward-facing harness must ride in a booster seat with a seat belt until age 9 or until the child outgrows the booster.
seat_belt_rule: A child who is at least 9, or has outgrown the booster, may use the seat belt alone if it fits: back against the seat, knees bent over the edge, lap belt low on the thighs and hips, shoulder belt across the chest and not the neck. All passengers under 18 must be restrained. When a child fits more than one stage, the more protective stage applies.
back_seat_rule: Children under 13 must ride in the rear seat when one is available. A child under 6 or under 60 pounds must ride in the rear seat if the vehicle has an active passenger-side airbag and a rear seat is available.
penalty: A violation is a petty misdemeanor with a fine of up to $50. The fine may be waived or reduced if the driver shows that, within 14 days, they bought or obtained a federally approved child restraint for their own use.
exemptions: Emergency medical vehicles; peace officers on duty (who must use a seat belt instead); drivers for hire such as taxis and buses; school buses over 10,000 pounds GVWR; and a child who, in a licensed physician's judgment, cannot safely ride in a restraint (the driver must carry a typewritten physician statement dated within the previous six months). Rental companies must provide a child restraint on request and may charge a reasonable fee.
agency: Minnesota Department of Public Safety, Office of Traffic Safety

summary: Children under 4 must ride in a child safety seat. Children 4 to 6 must use a belt-positioning booster if they are shorter than 4'9" or weigh less than 65 pounds.
rear_facing_rule: Mississippi law has no rear-facing requirement. The state health department recommends rear-facing seats.
harness_rule: A child under 4 must be protected by a child passenger restraint device or system that meets federal safety standards. The law doesn't say which type.
booster_rule: A child who is at least 4 but under 7 must use a belt-positioning booster seat if the child is shorter than 4 feet 9 inches or weighs less than 65 pounds. If more than two children need boosters and the rear seat has only two lap-and-shoulder belts, only the two children in those seats need boosters; the others may use a lap belt.
seat_belt_rule: At 7, or between 4 and 6 once the child is at least 4'9" and at least 65 pounds, the child moves to the seat belt. Mississippi's seat belt law (§ 63-2-1) requires every passenger in a passenger vehicle, in every seat, to wear a fastened belt.
back_seat_rule: No Mississippi law says where in the car a child must sit. The state health department advises children under 13 to ride in the back seat.
penalty: A violation of § 63-7-301 is punishable by a fine of not more than $25 for each offense (§ 63-7-309).
exemptions: The law covers passenger motor vehicles built to carry 15 or fewer people. It doesn't apply to vehicles excluded from the seat belt law: farm-use vehicles, implements of husbandry and farm tractors; passenger cars driven by rural mail carriers or utility meter readers on duty; and buses (§§ 63-7-301(2), 63-2-1(3)).
agency: Mississippi State Department of Health

summary: Children under 4, or under 40 pounds, must ride in a child safety seat. Children 4 to 7 who weigh 40 to 79 pounds and are under 4'9" must use a car seat or booster; once a child weighs 80 pounds or is taller than 4'9", a seat belt or booster is allowed.
rear_facing_rule: Missouri law has no rear-facing requirement.
harness_rule: Children under 4, regardless of weight, and children under 40 pounds, regardless of age, must be secured in a child passenger restraint system. MoDOT describes this as a rear-facing or forward-facing harness seat.
booster_rule: Children at least 4 but under 8 who weigh at least 40 but under 80 pounds and are shorter than 4'9" must be secured in a child passenger restraint system or booster seat. A child who would need a booster may ride with a lap belt only in a back seat that has no lap-and-shoulder belt for the booster.
seat_belt_rule: Children who weigh at least 80 pounds or are taller than 4'9" must be secured by a seat belt or a booster appropriate for the child. Drivers are responsible for restraining every passenger under 16 (§§ 307.178, 307.179).
back_seat_rule: No Missouri law requires children to ride in the back seat. When there are more children than seating positions, children who can't be restrained must ride behind the front seat if the vehicle has a back seat.
penalty: Violating the car seat or booster rules is an infraction with a fine of up to $50 plus court costs. The charge is dismissed or withdrawn if the driver shows, before or at the hearing, that they acquired the required seat. For a child who is 80 pounds or more or taller than 4'9", the penalty is the seat belt law's: a fine of up to $10, with no court costs and no points (§ 307.178.6).
exemptions: Public carriers for hire, and students 4 and older riding a school bus designed for 11 or more passengers that meets Missouri school bus standards.
agency: Missouri Department of Transportation (Missouri Coalition for Roadway Safety)

summary: Children under 2 must ride rear-facing; from 2 to 4, in a rear- or forward-facing seat with a harness; and from 4 to 8, in a forward-facing harnessed seat or a booster. A child moves to the adult seat belt at 9, or earlier after outgrowing the booster's height or weight limit.
rear_facing_rule: A child under 2 years of age must ride in a rear-facing child safety restraint that meets federal motor vehicle safety standards.
harness_rule: A child between 2 and up to 4 years of age must ride in a rear-facing or forward-facing child safety restraint with an internal harness.
booster_rule: A child between 4 and up to 8 years of age must ride in a forward-facing harnessed restraint or a booster seat used with a lap-and-shoulder belt. The adult belt is required at 9, or once the child outgrows the booster's manufacturer height or weight limits, whichever comes first.
seat_belt_rule: A passenger who is at least 9, or who has outgrown the booster's manufacturer height or weight limits (whichever comes first), must be secured with an adult seat belt. Every child restraint must be installed and used according to the manufacturer's instructions.
back_seat_rule: No Montana law says where in the car a child must sit.
penalty: A violation is punishable by a fine of up to $100. The fine must be waived if, within 7 days of the violation, the driver gives the charging officer's office proof of acquiring an appropriate child restraint. The waiver isn't available if a previous violation was already dismissed this way.
exemptions: Motor homes, school buses, taxicabs, farm tractors, bicycles, mopeds, quadricycles, motorcycles and motor-driven cycles; vehicles not federally required to have seat belts; ambulances and other authorized emergency vehicles; and an emergency that threatens the life of the driver or the child. The Department of Transportation may by rule exempt a child whose physical or medical condition or body size prevents use of a restraint.
agency: Montana Department of Transportation

summary: Children under 2 must ride rear-facing until they outgrow the seat's height or weight limit. All children under 8 must ride in a federally approved child safety seat in a back seat when one is available, and children 8 to 17 must wear a seat belt.
rear_facing_rule: All children up to 2 years of age must use a rear-facing child restraint until they outgrow the manufacturer's maximum height or weight for that seat.
harness_rule: Nebraska law sets no separate harness age. Children under 8 must use a federally approved child restraint, which can be a harnessed seat or a booster.
booster_rule: All children up to 8 years of age must ride in a child passenger restraint system that meets Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard 213 (a car seat or booster), correctly installed per the manufacturer's instructions.
seat_belt_rule: Children from 8 up to 18 must be secured by an occupant protection system (seat belt); NDOT says a booster also satisfies the law. This 8-to-18 rule is enforced only as a secondary action, after the driver is cited for something else.
back_seat_rule: Children under 8 must ride in a seat other than the front seat if that seat has a restraint system and isn't already taken by other children under 8.
penalty: A violation is an infraction with a $25 fine per violation, and failing to restrain several children at once counts as one offense (§ 60-6,268). NDOT says court costs are added and 1 point is assessed against the driver's record. The under-8 rules are primary enforcement.
exemptions: Taxicabs, mopeds, motorcycles, and vehicles of model year 1963 or earlier without occupant protection; a child whose physician certifies a restraint would be harmful because of weight, physical condition or another medical reason (the driver must carry a signed statement); drivers of authorized emergency vehicles on duty; and vehicles in a lawful parade or exhibition.
agency: Nebraska Department of Transportation, Highway Safety Office

summary: Children under 6 who are shorter than 57 inches must ride in a child restraint (car seat or booster), and children under 2 must ride rear-facing in the back seat. Passengers 6 and older, or 57 inches or taller, must wear a seat belt.
rear_facing_rule: A child under 2 must be secured in a rear-facing child restraint in the back seat. The child may ride rear-facing in the front passenger seat, with the airbag deactivated, only if a physician's signed statement says the child's special health care needs require it, if all back seats are taken by other children under 2, or if the vehicle has no back seat.
harness_rule: Nevada law sets no separate harness stage. A child under 6 and under 57 inches must use a child restraint appropriate for the child's size and weight.
booster_rule: A child under 6 years of age and less than 57 inches tall must be secured in a federally approved child restraint system appropriate for the child's size and weight, installed per the manufacturer's instructions. The law's definition includes booster seats.
seat_belt_rule: Passengers 6 or older, or 57 inches or taller regardless of age, must wear a seat belt in the front or back seat (NRS 484D.495). The driver is cited for an unbelted child under 18. Belt violations are enforced only after a stop for another violation, with a civil penalty of up to $25.
back_seat_rule: Children under 2 must ride rear-facing in the back seat, with the front-seat exceptions listed under rear-facing. There is no back-seat rule for older children.
penalty: A violation is a misdemeanor. First offense: $100–$500 fine or 10–50 hours of community service. Second: $500–$1,000 or 50–100 hours. Third or later: license suspension for 30 to 180 days. Completing a DPS-approved training program within 60 days of sentencing waives a first-offense fine or community service and halves a second-offense one. It is not a moving traffic violation, so no demerit points.
exemptions: Public transportation, including taxicabs, school buses and emergency vehicles; and a child whom a physician or advanced practice registered nurse finds a restraint would be impractical or dangerous for because of weight or physical or medical condition (a signed statement must be carried in the vehicle).
agency: Nevada Department of Public Safety, Office of Traffic Safety

summary: New Hampshire requires children under 2 to ride rear-facing and children under 7 to ride in a car seat or booster unless they are at least 57 inches tall. Everyone under 18 must be buckled up.
rear_facing_rule: A passenger under 2 must be secured in a rear-facing child restraint system that meets federal safety standards. The statute has no exception for a child who outgrows a rear-facing seat.
harness_rule: New Hampshire law has no separate harness stage. Children under 7 must ride in a federally approved child restraint, used within the maker's height and weight limits.
booster_rule: A passenger under 7 must be secured in a federally approved child restraint system, used according to the maker's instructions, including its height and weight limits. The rule doesn't apply once the child is 57 inches or taller.
seat_belt_rule: Passengers under 18 who are not in a child restraint must wear a properly adjusted and fastened seat belt. Drivers under 18 must also buckle up.
back_seat_rule: No New Hampshire law says where in the car a child must sit.
penalty: A violation carries a $50 fine for a first offense and $100 for a second or later offense. It is a violation, not a crime.
exemptions: The law doesn't apply to vehicles regularly used to carry passengers for hire, school buses over 10,000 pounds (or lighter school buses built without belts), a child whose individualized education program says restraints are contraindicated, vehicles made before 1968, motorcycles, antique vehicles, farm tractors, or parade vehicles going no more than 10 mph.
agency: New Hampshire Department of Safety, Office of Highway Safety

summary: New Jersey requires children under 8 and under 57 inches to ride in a car seat or booster in the back seat: rear-facing under 2 and 30 pounds, a five-point harness under 4 and 40 pounds, then a booster. Older children must wear a seat belt.
rear_facing_rule: A child under 2 and under 30 pounds must ride in a rear-facing seat with a five-point harness.
harness_rule: A child under 4 and under 40 pounds must ride in a rear-facing seat with a five-point harness until outgrowing its top height or weight limit, then in a forward-facing seat with a five-point harness.
booster_rule: A child under 8 and under 57 inches must ride in a forward-facing seat with a five-point harness until outgrowing its top height or weight limit, then in a belt-positioning booster seat.
seat_belt_rule: A child who is 8 or older, or under 8 but at least 57 inches tall, must wear a properly adjusted and fastened seat belt. The driver must make sure every passenger under 18 is belted.
back_seat_rule: Children under 8 and under 57 inches must ride in a rear seat. If the vehicle has no rear seat, the child may ride in front in a car seat or booster, but never in a rear-facing seat in front of a passenger airbag that is on.
penalty: A violation carries a fine of $50 to $75.
exemptions: The law covers motor vehicles equipped with seat belts or LATCH. It doesn't apply to school buses.
agency: New Jersey Division of Highway Traffic Safety

summary: New Mexico requires a rear-facing seat in the back seat under age 1, a child safety seat through age 4 (or under 40 pounds), and a booster or car seat for ages 5 and 6 (or under 60 pounds). Children 7 through 12 may use a car seat or a seat belt, and everyone under 18 must be restrained.
rear_facing_rule: Children under 1 must ride in a rear-facing child restraint that meets federal standards, in the rear seat if the vehicle has one.
harness_rule: Children 1 through 4, regardless of weight, and children under 40 pounds, regardless of age, must ride in a child passenger restraint device that meets federal standards. The statute doesn't say it must have a harness.
booster_rule: Children 5 and 6, regardless of weight, and children under 60 pounds, regardless of age, must ride in a booster seat or a child restraint that meets federal standards.
seat_belt_rule: Children 7 through 12 may use a child restraint or a seat belt. A child is properly belted when the lap belt lies across the thighs and hips, not the stomach, and the shoulder belt crosses the chest, not the neck. Every passenger under 18 must be in a child restraint or a seat belt.
back_seat_rule: A child under 1 must ride rear-facing in the rear seat if the vehicle has one. If there's no rear seat, the child may ride in front if the passenger airbag is deactivated or the vehicle has no deactivation switch.
penalty: The penalty assessment for a child not in a restraint device or seat belt is $25. The violation adds 2 points to the driver's license.
exemptions: Authorized emergency vehicles, public transportation and school buses are exempt. The rules also don't apply when every seating position with a seat belt is occupied.
agency: New Mexico Motor Vehicle Division

summary: New York requires children under 2 to ride rear-facing (unless they outgrow the seat), children under 4 to ride in a child safety seat, and children under 8 to ride in an appropriate child restraint such as a booster. Passengers 8 through 15 must wear a seat belt.
rear_facing_rule: A child under 2 must ride in a rear-facing child safety seat. If the child is taller or heavier than the seat maker's rear-facing limits, the seat may face forward.
harness_rule: Children under 4 must ride in a federally approved child safety seat. A child under 4 who weighs more than 40 pounds may instead use an appropriate child restraint system with the lap and shoulder belt, or a lap belt if no lap and shoulder belt is available.
booster_rule: Children 4 through 7 must ride in an appropriate child restraint system (a car seat or booster) used with the lap and shoulder belt, or a lap belt if no lap and shoulder belt is available. It is a defense to a ticket if the child is belted and is taller than 4'9" or heavier than 100 pounds.
seat_belt_rule: Passengers 8 through 15 must wear a seat belt in any seat, and the driver is responsible for them. Passengers 16 and older must also buckle up.
back_seat_rule: No New York law says where in the car a child must sit. The Governor's Traffic Safety Committee recommends the back seat for all children under 13.
penalty: A violation carries a civil fine of $25 to $100, plus 3 driver license points for a restraint violation involving a passenger under 16. For a child under 8, the court waives the fine if the driver shows they bought or rented a proper child restraint before the court date. The waiver doesn't apply to a second or later conviction.
exemptions: School buses and authorized emergency vehicles are outside the law, except fire vehicles and volunteer ambulances. A passenger or driver with a physical disability that prevents restraint use, certified by a physician or nurse practitioner, is exempt. Taxis, liveries and charter buses have separate, narrower rules.
agency: New York State Governor's Traffic Safety Committee

summary: North Carolina requires children under 8 and under 80 pounds to ride in a weight-appropriate car seat or booster, and children under 5 and under 40 pounds to ride in the back seat when the car has an active front passenger airbag. All passengers under 16 must be buckled up.
rear_facing_rule: North Carolina law does not require rear-facing.
harness_rule: North Carolina law has no separate harness stage. Children under 8 and under 80 pounds must ride in a weight-appropriate child passenger restraint system.
booster_rule: A child under 8 and under 80 pounds must be properly secured in a weight-appropriate child passenger restraint system. The requirement ends when the child turns 8 or reaches 80 pounds.
seat_belt_rule: Passengers under 16 must be secured in a child restraint or a seat belt. If no seat with a lap and shoulder belt is available for the car seat, a child under 8 who weighs 40 to 80 pounds may use a properly fitted lap belt alone.
back_seat_rule: In a vehicle with an active passenger-side front airbag and a rear seat, a child under 5 and under 40 pounds must ride in the rear seat, unless the child restraint is designed for use with airbags.
penalty: A violation carries a fine of up to $25, even if more than one child was unsecured, plus 2 driver license points and no insurance points. A driver charged over a child under 8 can't be convicted if they show the court they have since gotten an approved child restraint for the vehicle the child usually rides in.
exemptions: The law doesn't apply to ambulances or other emergency vehicles, when every seating position with a child restraint or seat belt is occupied, or to vehicles that federal law doesn't require to have seat belts.
agency: North Carolina Governor's Highway Safety Program (NCDOT)

summary: Children under 8 must ride in a car seat or booster used per the manufacturer's instructions unless they are at least 4'9" tall, in which case a seat belt is enough. Ages 8 through 17 must use a seat belt or a child restraint.
rear_facing_rule: No rear-facing requirement in state law.
harness_rule: No separate harness stage in law. A child under 8 must be in a child restraint system (car seat or booster) used per the manufacturer's instructions.
booster_rule: A child under 8 must be in a child restraint system (car seat or booster). A child under 8 who is at least 57 inches (4'9") tall is not required to use one but must be correctly buckled in a safety belt.
seat_belt_rule: Children 8 through 17 must be in an approved child restraint or correctly buckled in a safety belt. A child under 8 who is at least 4'9" may use a seat belt.
back_seat_rule: No back-seat requirement in law. The state health department recommends children under 13 ride in the back.
penalty: $25 fee (N.D.C.C. § 39-06.1-06) and 1 point against the driver's license (§ 39-06.1-10). The driver is responsible.
exemptions: Does not apply in vehicles that were not equipped with safety belts when manufactured, or when a child is transported in an emergency.
agency: North Dakota Health and Human Services

summary: Children under 4 or under 40 pounds must ride in a car seat, and children under 8 who are shorter than 4'9" must ride in a booster. Children 8 through 15 must use a car seat or a seat belt.
rear_facing_rule: No rear-facing requirement in state law.
harness_rule: A child who is under 4 years old or weighs under 40 pounds must be secured in a child restraint system that meets federal standards, per the manufacturer's instructions.
booster_rule: A child under 8 and under 4'9" who no longer needs a car seat must be secured on a booster seat that meets federal standards.
seat_belt_rule: Children 8 through 15 must be restrained in a child restraint system or a seat belt. Police may not stop a driver solely for a booster (age 4-7) or age 8-15 belt violation; those rules are secondary enforcement.
back_seat_rule: No back-seat requirement in law.
penalty: First offense is a minor misdemeanor with a fine of $25 to $75; a repeat offense is a fourth-degree misdemeanor. Several unrestrained children at the same time and place count as one violation. Fines go to the child highway safety fund.
exemptions: Taxicabs and public safety vehicles; emergencies that threaten life; a child with a physical impairment documented by an affidavit from a physician, clinical nurse specialist, certified nurse practitioner or chiropractor (the child must be restrained as the affidavit recommends). Child care center and nursery school vehicles follow their own rule.

summary: Children under 2 ride rear-facing (or until they outgrow the rear-facing seat) and children under 4 ride in a car seat. Children 4 to 7 who are not taller than 4'9" must use a car seat or booster; at 8, or once taller than 4'9", a seat belt is enough.
rear_facing_rule: The child restraint must be rear-facing until the child turns 2 or reaches the rear-facing seat's height or weight limit, whichever comes first.
harness_rule: A child under 4 must be properly secured in a child passenger restraint system.
booster_rule: A child at least 4 but younger than 8, if not taller than 4'9", must be secured in a child passenger restraint system or booster seat.
seat_belt_rule: If a child is 8 or taller than 4'9", a properly secured seat belt meets the law. The general belt law (47 O.S. § 12-417) covers drivers and front-seat passengers.
back_seat_rule: No back-seat requirement in law.
penalty: $50 fine plus court costs. For a first offense the fine is suspended and court costs are capped at $15 with proof of buying or borrowing a child restraint. The Department of Public Safety may not assess points.
exemptions: School buses, taxicabs, mopeds, motorcycles and vehicles not required to have belts; ambulances and emergency vehicles; vehicles with all belts in use; children with a physician's written medical exemption; a child over 40 pounds in a back seat with only lap belts (or when the lap-shoulder belts are used by other children over 40 pounds); and forward-facing use for a child under 4 by a driver with a disability placard or plate and a DPS forward-facing exemption letter.
agency: Oklahoma State Department of Health, Injury Prevention Service

summary: Children under 2 must ride rear-facing and children 40 pounds or less must ride in a car seat. Children over 40 pounds must use a booster until they are taller than 4'9" or turn 8.
rear_facing_rule: A person under 2 years of age must be secured with a child safety system in a rear-facing position.
harness_rule: A child who weighs 40 pounds or less must be secured in a child safety system designed for children 40 pounds or less.
booster_rule: A child over 40 pounds who is 4'9" or shorter must use a child safety system that raises the child so the belt fits (a booster). From age 8 a child may use a seat belt instead.
seat_belt_rule: A person taller than 4'9", or any child 8 or older, must be secured with a safety belt or harness. The driver is responsible for passengers under 16.
back_seat_rule: No back-seat requirement in law (ODOT). A rear-facing seat cannot go in front of an active airbag.
penalty: Class D traffic violation: presumptive fine $115, maximum $250 (ORS 153.019, 153.018).
exemptions: Booster rule does not apply in a rear seat with only lap belts (if the child uses the lap belt) or if the child uses a harness seat rated over 40 pounds. ORS 811.215 lists other exemptions, including for-hire vehicles' child seat duty, vehicles not required to have belts, a DMV medical exemption certificate (ORS 811.220), and when all seating positions are occupied.
agency: Oregon Department of Transportation

summary: Children under 2 must ride rear-facing and children under 4 must ride in a car seat. Children 4 to 7 must ride in a booster, and children 8 to 17 must wear a seat belt.
rear_facing_rule: A child under 2 must be fastened in a rear-facing child passenger restraint system, used until the child outgrows the manufacturer's maximum weight and height limits.
harness_rule: A child under 4 must be fastened in a child passenger restraint system anywhere in the vehicle, including the cargo area.
booster_rule: A child 4 or older but under 8 must be fastened in a seat belt and an appropriately fitting booster seat. There is no height exemption.
seat_belt_rule: The driver must secure every occupant 8 or older but under 18 in a properly adjusted seat belt.
back_seat_rule: No back-seat requirement in law. PennDOT recommends the back seat through age 12.
penalty: Summary offense with a $75 fine for car seat or booster violations; the 8-17 belt rule carries a $10 fine. Not a moving violation. Charges are dismissed if the driver shows the judge proof of acquiring a child seat or booster before or at the hearing. Insurers may not raise premiums for a conviction.
exemptions: PennDOT may grant exemptions when a car seat or booster is impractical for physical reasons, including medical reasons or the child's size.
agency: Pennsylvania Department of Transportation

summary: Children under 2 or under 30 pounds must ride rear-facing, and children under 8 who are under 57 inches and under 80 pounds must ride in a car seat or booster in a rear seat. All children under 8 ride in a rear seat, and children 8 to 17 must wear a seat belt.
rear_facing_rule: All infants and toddlers under 2 or weighing less than 30 pounds must be restrained in a rear-facing car seat.
harness_rule: Not required as a separate stage. The law says children 2 and older, or who have outgrown the rear-facing seat, should use a forward-facing harnessed seat up to the manufacturer's maximum.
booster_rule: A child under 8, under 57 inches and under 80 pounds must ride in a federally approved child restraint system in a rear seating position.
seat_belt_rule: A child under 8 who is at least 57 inches or at least 80 pounds must wear a seat belt in a rear seat. Children 8 to 17 must wear a seat belt in any seat.
back_seat_rule: Children under 8 must ride in a rear seating position. They may ride in front, properly restrained, only if the vehicle has no back seat or all rear seats are used by other children.
penalty: $100 under the state violation schedule (§ 31-41.1-4) for no child restraint or for a child not in a rear seat; $40 for a passenger 8-17 without a belt. A child restraint citation is voided if proof of buying an approved seat is shown to the issuing police department within 7 days. Violations are not recorded on the driving record.
exemptions: Front-seat placement is allowed if there is no back seat or all rear positions are used by other children. The 8-17 belt rule does not apply to pre-July 1966 vehicles, vehicles not required to have belts, a person with a physician's written verification (up to 12 months), or postal letter carriers on duty.

summary: Children under 2 ride rear-facing and then in a harnessed forward-facing seat until they outgrow it; children 4 and up who have outgrown the harness use a booster until age 8 or 57 inches and a proper belt fit. Children under 8 must ride in the back seat.
rear_facing_rule: A child under 2 must ride in a rear-facing seat in a rear seat until the child exceeds the seat's height or weight limit.
harness_rule: A child 2 or older (or under 2 who has outgrown rear-facing) must ride in a forward-facing harnessed seat in a rear seat until exceeding the seat's highest height or weight limit. Only a child at least 4 who has outgrown it may move to a booster.
booster_rule: A child at least 4 who has outgrown the forward-facing seat must use a belt-positioning booster with a lap and shoulder belt in a rear seat until meeting the adult-belt height and fit requirements.
seat_belt_rule: A child at least 8 or at least 57 inches tall may use an adult belt if it fits: lap belt across the thighs and hips, shoulder belt across the center of the chest, and knees bent at the seat edge without slouching. Drivers must make occupants 17 and under wear a belt or ride in a child restraint.
back_seat_rule: Children under 8 must ride in a rear seat. They may ride in front, in the proper seat, only if there is no rear seat or all rear seats are occupied by children under 8.
penalty: Fine of not more than $150. The court must waive the fine if, before or on the court date, the driver shows proof of acquiring, buying or renting an appropriate child restraint.
exemptions: Taxi drivers; emergency vehicles in an emergency; church, day care and school bus drivers; public transportation; commercial vehicles. A child with a documented medical need (physician, advanced nurse practitioner or physician assistant) may use a restraint designed for that need.
agency: South Carolina Department of Public Safety

summary: Children under 5 must ride in a child restraint system, unless they weigh at least 40 pounds, in which case a seat belt is enough. Passengers 5 to 17 must wear a seat belt.
rear_facing_rule: No rear-facing requirement in state law.
harness_rule: A child under 5 must be secured in a child passenger restraint system per the manufacturer's instructions. A child under 5 who weighs at least 40 pounds may use a seat belt instead.
booster_rule: No booster seat requirement in state law.
seat_belt_rule: The driver must make sure passengers at least 5 and under 18 wear a properly adjusted seat belt. Drivers and passengers 14 to 17 must also wear one themselves.
back_seat_rule: No back-seat requirement in law.
penalty: A violation is a petty offense (handled as a civil proceeding). The statute does not set the fine amount.
exemptions: Does not apply in passenger cars made before 1966 that were not equipped with seat belts.

summary: Children under 1 or 20 pounds or less ride rear-facing; ages 1 through 3 over 20 pounds ride in a harnessed car seat; ages 4 through 8 under 4'9" ride in a booster, all in the rear seat if available. Children 9 through 12, or any child 12 or younger who is 4'9" or taller, must use a seat belt.
rear_facing_rule: Children under 1, or any child weighing 20 pounds or less, must ride in a rear-facing child restraint in the rear seat if available.
harness_rule: Children 1 through 3 weighing more than 20 pounds must ride in a harnessed child safety seat (rear- or forward-facing) in the rear seat if available.
booster_rule: Children 4 through 8 who are shorter than 4'9" must ride in a belt-positioning booster in the rear seat if available.
seat_belt_rule: Children 9 through 12, or any child 12 or younger who is 4'9" or taller, must use a seat belt; the rear seat is recommended. Children 13 through 15 must use a seat belt.
back_seat_rule: Children in rear-facing, harnessed or booster seats (through age 8) must ride in the rear seat if available. The rear seat is recommended, not required, for ages 9 through 12.
penalty: Each unrestrained child 8 or younger is a separate violation, with court costs; the statute makes it a Class C misdemeanor, and a court may order a first offender to attend a child passenger safety class. For the age 9-12 belt rule, only one citation per vehicle is issued: a $50 fine with no court costs or litigation taxes.
exemptions: A child who cannot safely use a standard restraint may use a specially modified one if the driver carries a physician's signed prescription.
agency: Tennessee Highway Safety Office

summary: Children younger than 8 must ride in a child safety seat or booster, used per the manufacturer's instructions, unless they are taller than 4'9". Children 8 to 16 must wear a seat belt.
rear_facing_rule: No rear-facing requirement in state law.
harness_rule: No separate harness stage in law. A child under 8 must be in a child passenger safety seat system per the manufacturer's instructions.
booster_rule: A child younger than 8 must be secured in a child passenger safety seat system (car seat or booster) unless the child is taller than 4'9".
seat_belt_rule: A child younger than 17 who is not required to be in a child seat must be secured by a seat belt in any belted seat. Passengers 15 and older are personally responsible for buckling up.
back_seat_rule: No back-seat requirement in law.
penalty: Misdemeanor with a fine of $25 to $250. It is a defense if the driver had no child seat in the vehicle, was not cited for anything else, was not in a crash, and later obtains an appropriate seat.
exemptions: Defense if driving in an emergency or for a law enforcement purpose. Does not apply to vehicles transporting passengers for hire (except contracted non-emergency Medicaid transport), or when all seating positions with belts or child seats are occupied.
agency: Texas Department of Transportation

summary: Children younger than 8 must ride in a child restraint device used per the manufacturer's instructions, unless they are 57 inches or taller. Children 8 to 15 must wear a seat belt.
rear_facing_rule: No rear-facing requirement in state law.
harness_rule: No separate harness stage in law. A child under 8 must be in a child restraint device used per the manufacturer's instructions.
booster_rule: Each person younger than 8 must be in a child restraint device (car seat or booster). A child under 8 who is 57 inches or taller is exempt and must wear a seat belt.
seat_belt_rule: The driver must secure each child 8 and older (and under 16) in a properly adjusted seat belt. Passengers 16 and older must buckle up themselves.
back_seat_rule: No back-seat requirement in law.
penalty: Infraction with a maximum fine of $45. The court must waive the whole fine for a first child-restraint violation with proof of acquiring, renting or buying a child restraint. No points. Several unrestrained occupants count as one offense.
exemptions: Vehicles made before July 1, 1966 or not required to have belts; a person with a physician or physician assistant's written verification; a passenger when all seats are occupied; public transit vehicles over 10,000 pounds. In a taxi or rideshare, the supervising adult passenger is responsible for the child's restraint.
agency: Utah Highway Safety Office

summary: Children under 2 must ride rear-facing with a harness, children under 5 in a harnessed seat (rear- or forward-facing), and children under 8 in a booster if not in a harnessed seat. Children under 18 must otherwise wear a seat belt, and children under 13 ride in the back seat when practical.
rear_facing_rule: A child under 2 must be secured in a federally approved rear-facing child restraint with a harness.
harness_rule: A child under 5 not in a rear-facing seat must be in a forward-facing harnessed seat until reaching the seat's weight or height limit.
booster_rule: A child under 8 who is not in a harnessed car seat must be secured in a booster seat. There is no height exemption.
seat_belt_rule: A child under 18 who is not in a harnessed seat or booster must be restrained in a seat belt.
back_seat_rule: A child under 13 must always, if practical, ride in a rear seat. A rear-facing seat may not be placed in front of an active passenger airbag.
penalty: Civil penalty of $25 for a first violation, $50 for a second, and $100 for a third or later violation.
exemptions: Type I school buses; vehicles regularly used to carry passengers for hire (except child care facility vehicles); vehicles manufactured without belts; and evacuations ordered by an enforcement officer, firefighter or civil authority.
agency: Vermont Department of Health (Be Seat Smart)

summary: Children up to age 8 must ride in a child safety seat, rear-facing until at least age 2 (or until reaching the seat maker's minimum forward-facing weight), in the back seat. Passengers under 18 must otherwise wear a seat belt.
rear_facing_rule: A child restraint may not face forward until the child reaches 2 years of age or the minimum weight for a forward-facing seat set by its manufacturer.
harness_rule: No separate harness stage in law. A child under 8 must be in a child restraint device that meets federal standards, chosen per the manufacturer's instructions.
booster_rule: Any child up to age 8 (through age 7) must be secured in a federally approved child restraint device (car seat or booster). There is no height exemption.
seat_belt_rule: Anyone transporting a person under 18 who is not required to be in a child restraint must make sure that person is properly secured by a seat belt.
back_seat_rule: Child restraint devices must be placed in the back seat. If the vehicle has no back seat, the seat may go in the front passenger seat only if there is no passenger airbag or it has been deactivated.
penalty: $50 civil penalty, not suspendable, for a first violation; up to $500 for a second or later violation on a different date. No demerit points and no court costs. The court may waive the penalty if the driver could not afford a child seat. Fines go to the Child Restraint Device Special Fund.
exemptions: Taxicabs, school buses, executive sedans and limousines. A child exempted by a physician (weight, height, physical unfitness or medical reason) must carry the signed statement; failing to carry it is a $20 penalty. Emergency and law enforcement vehicles under exigent circumstances when no seat is available.
agency: Virginia Department of Health

summary: Children under 2 ride rear-facing and children under 4 ride in a harnessed seat until they outgrow it; after that, children ride in a booster until they are 4'9" tall. Children under 13 ride in the back seat where practical.
rear_facing_rule: A child under 2 must be in a rear-facing child restraint until reaching the seat's weight or height limit.
