harness_rule: A child under 4 who is not rear-facing must be in a forward-facing harnessed seat until reaching the seat's weight or height limit.
booster_rule: A child who is not in a rear-facing or harnessed seat and is under 4'9" must be in a booster seat (there is no age cutoff). The booster rule does not apply where only a lap belt is available.
seat_belt_rule: A child under 16 who has outgrown the booster stage must be secured with a properly adjusted and fastened seat belt.
back_seat_rule: A driver transporting a child under 13 must use the back seat where it is practical to do so.
penalty: Traffic infraction. Child restraint violations are not listed in the court penalty schedule, so the default base penalty of $48 plus statutory assessments applies (local court rules may differ). The ticket is dismissed if the driver shows proof of getting an approved child seat or booster within 7 days and has never had one dismissed before.
exemptions: For-hire vehicles; auto transportation company vehicles for 16 or fewer passengers; parking, hotel, convention and airport shuttles; school buses. The booster rule does not apply in seats with only a lap belt.

summary: Children under 8 must ride in a child passenger safety seat (car seat or booster) unless they are at least 4'9" tall, in which case a seat belt is enough. Passengers under 18 in the back seat and everyone in front must wear a belt.
rear_facing_rule: No rear-facing requirement in state law.
harness_rule: No separate harness stage in law. A child under 8 must be in a federally approved child passenger safety device.
booster_rule: A child under 8 must be in a federally approved child passenger safety device system (which includes a booster). If the child is under 8 and at least 4'9" tall, a seat belt meets the law.
seat_belt_rule: The driver, every front-seat passenger, and back-seat passengers under 18 must wear a seat belt (W. Va. Code § 17C-15-49, $25 fine, no points).
back_seat_rule: No back-seat requirement in law.
penalty: Misdemeanor with a fine of $10 to $20.
exemptions: Vehicles operated for hire. A driver is not in violation if every seat belt is in use and there are more passengers than belts.
agency: West Virginia Governor's Highway Safety Program

summary: Children under 1 or under 20 pounds ride rear-facing, and children under 4 or under 40 pounds ride in a rear- or forward-facing car seat, in the back seat if there is one. Children 4 to 7 who weigh 40 to 80 pounds and are 4'9" or shorter ride in a car seat or booster.
rear_facing_rule: A child less than 1 year old, or less than 20 pounds, must be in a rear-facing child seat in the back seat (if the vehicle has one).
harness_rule: A child at least 1 and 20 pounds but under 4 or under 40 pounds must be in a forward- or rear-facing child seat in the back seat (if the vehicle has one).
booster_rule: A child from age 4 to 8 who weighs 40 to 80 pounds and is no more than 4'9" must be in a child seat or a booster seat.
seat_belt_rule: All drivers and passengers over age 4 must wear seat belts; drivers are responsible for unbelted passengers 4 to 16.
back_seat_rule: Children who must ride in a rear- or forward-facing car seat (under 4 or under 40 pounds) must be in the back seat if the vehicle has one. The booster stage has no back-seat rule.
penalty: WisDOT lists the total penalty as $175.30 if the child is under 4, and $150.10 for a first offense, $200.50 for a second and $263.50 for a third or later offense if the child is 4 to 8. The base forfeiture is $30-$75 (under 4) or $10-$25 (ages 4-8).
exemptions: WisDOT says no exemption allows taking a child out of the restraint for personal needs such as feeding or diapering. Statutory exemptions were not confirmed.
agency: Wisconsin Department of Transportation

summary: Children under 9 must ride in a child safety restraint, in a seat other than the front seat when possible, unless the vehicle's lap and shoulder belt fits them properly. Every passenger must wear a seat belt, and drivers must buckle up passengers under 12.
rear_facing_rule: No rear-facing requirement in state law. A rear-facing infant seat may not be placed in front of an active airbag.
harness_rule: No separate harness stage in law. A child under 9 must be in a child safety restraint system used per the manufacturer's instructions.
booster_rule: Each child who has not reached their ninth birthday must be secured in a child safety restraint system (car seat or booster). The exception: a child whose lap and shoulder belt fits properly across the collarbone, chest and hips.
seat_belt_rule: Every driver and passenger must wear a seat belt, and the driver must make sure passengers under 12 wear one. A child under 9 may use the belt alone only if it fits properly.
back_seat_rule: Children under 9 must ride in a seat other than the front seat. They may ride in front if the vehicle has only one row of seats or all rear belts are used by other child passengers.
penalty: Fine of up to $50 for a first offense, waived if the driver shows the court they bought, leased or got a proper restraint after the offense. Up to $100 for a second or later offense. Using a restraint against the manufacturer's instructions is also a violation.
exemptions: A child with a physician's signed statement (carried in the vehicle) that the child's weight or condition requires not using a restraint; a driver giving aid to the child or parent; a child whose lap and shoulder belt fits properly. The law does not cover emergency and law enforcement vehicles, school buses (including private school or church buses used for school or church trips), or public transportation buses built without belts.
